review.summary: Slice reviewed: app.css, dialogs.css, claink.css, the build's notices, verify.mjs and the browser gates (actions, phone, layout, fixtures). Both gates passed twice with no check changing result: actions.cjs 104/104, phone.cjs 55/55. lint-css and lint-copy are clean. I measured the 2.1.1 build against Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.html at all the requested sizes and at the clamp boundaries. The main screen holds well, and End week now stays on screen wherever 2.1 lost it. I found five real problems, none of them serious. (1) On clAInk's policy step, the longer terms push the 40px Accept button below the ad's visible area at the narrowest, shortest desktop windows (1025 to 1050 wide, 620 to 660 tall); 2.1 fit there. (2) The release header credits Feather for 10 icons, but there are 11: the bundled `triangle-alert` is Feather's `alert-triangle` under a new name. (3) The claim that no hint needs a third line is false: the "+N" chip's hint can need three, and the actions gate's §8 never points at that chip. (4) QA §4.1 understates how far End week still hangs below the week card's bottom edge at widths 1025 to 1190. (5) The stacked tier's tighter caption line spacing also reaches upright phones. My probe scripts are in test-results/review/layout/ (rv-*.cjs and probe-main.cjs). The folder is shared with another reviewer, so the files not prefixed rv- are mostly theirs.
checked_ok: The clamp() arithmetic is right at the boundaries. The card's padding and gaps reach their 8px floor at 640px tall, and the action rows reach 43.4px at about 660px. The hint bar is two lines with no padding at 625px tall and below, and gets its full padding from 641px. Across the width it does the same between 1180px and 1212px. Measured at 1366 wide by 620, 625, 633, 641, 657, 700, 746 and 772 tall, and at 1180, 1196 and 1212 wide by 700 and 768 tall: End week is inside the card and the window everywhere 1212px wide and up.
`--short` is set on `.left`, and every element that uses it (`.kpi`, `.quarter`, `.stats`, `.actions`, `.hint`) is inside `.left` (Board.jsx). So no rule falls back to its initial value.

Compared with 2.1, End week is at the same pixel at 1280x800, 1440x900, 1536x864, 1920x1080, 2560x1440 and 1366x772, and 0.6px lower at 1366x746. At heights of 864 and more the sections above it sit 2 to 3px higher because the hint bar is taller; nothing is cut and nothing scrolls.

The stacked tier at rest is unchanged from 2.1 at 1024x768, 768x1024, 1093x614 (125% zoom) and 911x512 (150% zoom), apart from the cash card's line, which is now level as intended. A 390x844 phone is identical. On a 360x640 phone the action grid is 17px taller because a longer cost line wraps; that copy is outside this slice.
Stat cards: the second line is level across all four cards at every size measured. The cash card never has a meter (Kpis.jsx), so its 8px margin is safe.
Recovery dialog: at 320, 360, 375 and 390px every button is on the screen (in 2.1 the left edges were at -42/-56, -2/-16, -1 and 14). Nothing changes at 412px and up or at 641 and 700px wide.
Handbook statement: in the footer above 1024px wide (two lines; footer still 64px tall, 67px at 1920) and in the body below that. The handbook still fits 1440x900 without scrolling.

The landscape 2x2 rule for the ending's tiles only applies to windows up to 1024 wide and up to 600 tall. The 2.1.1 build has no `.d` chips missing, and actions §7's log-chip check fails on 2.1, which has no per-chip `.d` spans, so that check is not vacuous.

Release file header: a well-formed comment (ASCII only, no `--` inside, no CR). The charset declaration is at byte 884 of 1024, the page runs in standards mode (CSS1Compat) as UTF-8, the release file is byte-identical to dist/index.html, and scheduler is named.

clAInk policy step: fits, with no overlap, at 1280x620, 1366x620, 1366x657, 1200x620, 1440x900, 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 1024x768, 768x1024 and 1093x614. The new `headline` drop step does nothing on the pitch step (the CSS only hides the headline while confirming), so the pitch's fit is unchanged from 2.1.

Gates run twice each: actions 104/104 both times (21:39 to 21:42 and 21:42 to 21:44), phone 55/55 both times; no check changed result. The detail lines that differed were dice values: deals moved, Recharge amounts, the clAInk invoice ($1,349 vs $620), and whether usage and Cancel seat were in sight at 1366x650. The §6 'Close deals ... pressed' check tested nothing in run 2 because the deal neither signed nor walked. The code marks that check as not certain, and the Recharge and Proposals checks cover the same fix deterministically.

phone.cjs §10: the edge tap runs with scripted dice (`__TST_RNG = () => 0.95`), so it is deterministic. The caption check covers the four longest top-bar lines (69, 62, 59 and 55 characters). The recovery and caption checks fail on 2.1 as they should, judging by my 2.1 measurements.
lint-css OK (0 findings); lint-copy OK (0 violations).

findings.title: clAInk's policy step hides its Accept button below the ad's visible area at narrow, short desktop windows, where 2.1 showed it whole
findings.where: src/styles/claink.css (the new `tight` and `headline` fit rules for the policy step) together with the five-item policy list; the gate's sizes are in test/e2e/lib/fixtures.cjs VIEWPORTS
findings.evidence: Probe test-results/review/layout/rv-policy.cjs: save ck-ad-week-3, click .claink-cta, then measure. In 2.1.1 at 1025x640 and 1050x640, data-fit is 'tight announce chips badges proof headline' (every optional part dropped), the ad scrolls, and 16px of the 40px .claink-confirm button is below the ad's visible bottom (3px below the window). At 1025x620 it is 29px below, at 1025x650 9px, at 1025x660 2px. In 2.1 at 1025x640, 1050x640 and 1025x660 the ad does not scroll (data-fit 'tight announce') and the button has 20px to spare; at 1025x620 2.1 scrolls too but its button is still inside the ad (16px clear). 2.1.1 fits again at 1075x640 and at every gated size, so QA item 19's 'fits its corner at every gated size' is literally true. But no gated size is this narrow and short, and the regression is not listed in §4.
findings.proposal: Add a narrow, short size such as 1025x640 to the layout gate's dock-whole sizes. Then either let the policy step close up further at that size (for example the policy header line or the gaps between terms), or record it in §4 next to §4.1.

findings.title: The release header credits Feather for 10 icons; 11 of the bundled icons are Feather-derived
findings.where: scripts/build.mjs notices() (`ours = iconNames.filter(n => derived.has(n))`); line 8 of Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.1.html; TTST_2.1.1_QA_REPORT.md item 32 and §9; CHANGELOG.md
findings.evidence: Lucide's LICENSE lists its Feather-derived icons by their old names. The build matches bundled icons against that list by name, which finds 10: arrow-right, calendar, check, compass, info, loader, lock, minus, search, x. The game also bundles `triangle-alert` (src/ui uses icon: "triangle-alert"; it is in the 56 bundled symbols). That is Lucide's new name for `alert-triangle`, which is on the Feather list, and node_modules/lucide-static/icons/alert-triangle.svg has exactly the same path data as triangle-alert.svg (only the class attribute differs). I compared every bundled icon not matched by name against every listed icon's file; triangle-alert was the only match. So the header line '10 of them derived from Feather' should read 11. The audit (qa/2.1.1/audit/hygiene.json) counted by name and missed it too, and the notices gate does not check this count.
findings.proposal: In notices(), also count a bundled icon whose SVG body is identical to the file of a listed name (lucide-static ships the alias files), or keep a small alias map; rebuild so the header says 11. Correct 'ten' in QA item 32, QA §9 and the CHANGELOG.

findings.title: 'No hint needs a third line at any width' is false: the '+N' chip's hint takes three lines at 1025 wide, and actions §8 never points at that chip
findings.where: src/styles/app.css, the comment on the `.hint` height rule (the line citing actions.cjs section 8); test/e2e/actions.cjs §8, whose target list holds only [data-act] cards, the Hail Mary and End week; TTST_2.1.1_QA_REPORT.md item 12
findings.evidence: Probe rv-chiphint.cjs. State: competitor match (odds and a discount), case study, conference buzz, full funnel, PIP level 2, 2 quad shots, a trip, rested; 9 chips in all. At 1025x768 one chip shows and '+8' holds the rest. Pointing at '+8' puts 54.6px of text (three lines: '8 more. Discount 20% · this week · Close odds +8 pp · …') in the bar, which now has a fixed height of 38.4px. The text runs from 653.3 to 707.8 while the bar spans 661.3 to 699.7, so it spills 8px over the bar's top and bottom borders. At 1180x768, 1280x720 and 1366x657 the same hint is two lines and fits. 2.1 overflowed the same way (its bar shrank to its 36px minimum), so this is not a regression. But the comment and QA item 12 say no hint needs a third line and that §8 holds that, and §8 cannot see this hint.
findings.proposal: Add '.chip.more' to §8's targets with a state that folds many chips, at 1025x768. Then either keep the folded-chip summary to two lines (for example a count only beyond N names) or limit the claim to the action, Hail Mary and End week hints.

findings.title: QA §4.1 understates the remaining problem: at 1025 to 1190 wide, End week hangs below the week card at every height up to about 765px, not only under 660px
findings.where: TTST_2.1.1_QA_REPORT.md §4.1 (and item 11's 'At 746px and above nothing moves'); the desktop clamp() rules in src/styles/app.css; test/e2e/lib/fixtures.cjs VIEWPORTS (no size between 1025 and 1199 wide)
findings.evidence: Probe rv-grid.cjs on midrun-seeded measures how far End week's bottom edge is below the week card's bottom edge. 1025x660: 6.1px. 1025x700: 7.6. 1100x720: 8.4. 1025x740: 9.1. 1025x746: 9.5. 1190x746: 12.0. 1025x760: 0.7. Gone by 770. At 1190x620, 20.9px of the 36px button is below the window; at 1200x620, 4px. Both widths are above §4.1's 'under about 1,180px'; the stat cards are still wrapped at 1190 (152.8px tall against 119px from 1212). §4.1 says the button hangs below the card's edge only 'if the window is also under about 660px tall'. Item 11 counts the same kind of hang (9px at 1280x720) as the 2.1 defect this release fixed. Not a regression: 2.1 is worse at every one of these sizes (at 1025x700 its End week is 50.9px past the window). Only the stated extent is wrong, and no gated size reaches this band (1200x800 and 1280x620 are both fine).
findings.proposal: Restate §4.1 as roughly '1,025 to about 1,200px wide and 620 to about 765px tall: End week hangs up to 12px below the card's edge, and below 640px it is partly cut by the window'. Optionally add 1100x700 to the layout gate as a known expected failure so the residue is tracked.

findings.title: The stacked tier's caption line height (1.2) also applies to upright phones' bottom notice, which the phone tier meant to keep as it was
findings.where: src/styles/app.css stacked tier `.pa-cap{white-space:normal;line-height:1.2}` (line 235); the phone tier resets `.pa-text` (line 281) but not `.pa-cap`'s line-height
findings.evidence: Probe rv-dialogs.cjs caption on touch phones, raising each line with TST_AUDIO.say. At 390x844 and 360x640 the caption's computed line-height is 18.2px in 2.1 and 15.6px in 2.1.1. Two-line notices (whale, meetings, sqlStorm, freeze) shrink from 54.4px to 51.2px. QA item 17 scopes this change to the top bar on an upright tablet and a phone held sideways. On an upright phone the caption is a separate notice at the foot of the screen, and the phone tier's own reset (display:block, overflow:visible, line-clamp none) shows it was meant to stay as in 2.1. Cosmetic only; nothing is cut.
findings.proposal: Add line-height:1.4 to the phone tier's `.pa-cap` rule, or scope the 1.2 to `.topbar .pa-cap` in the stacked tier.

verdicts.title: clAInk's policy step hides its Accept button below the ad's visible area at narrow, short desktop windows, where 2.1 showed it whole
verdicts.why: Reproduced with my own probes on Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.1.html (same bytes as dist/index.html), using ck-ad-week-3 and clicking .claink-cta (test-results/review/layout-check/policy.cjs, policy-scan.cjs). With Playwright's hidden scrollbars, at 1025x640 and 1040x640 data-fit is 'tight announce chips badges proof headline', the ad overflows by 36px, and Accept's bottom is 15.6px below the ad's visible bottom (2.6px below the window). At 1025x620 the overflow is 49px and the button is 28.6px below. Only its top 11px shows and the label is hidden (picture ad-Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.1-1025x620.png). It is 8.6px below at 1025x650 and 1.6px at 1025x660, and whole from 1025x665 and from 1055x640. In 2.1 the same sizes do not scroll and Accept has 20px to spare; at 620px 2.1 scrolls 4px with Accept 15.7px clear. With Chrome's classic scrollbars turned on (policy-scan-bars.cjs, as on Windows) the band is wider: at 1025x640 Accept is 33.8px below (about 6px of 40 visible), 5.8px below at 1025x680 and 15.6px at 1060x640, while 2.1 stays clear everywhere. Focus goes to 'Not now' with preventScroll, so the step opens in this clipped state. The ad scrolls, and Tab reaches the button. Cause: item 19's two extra terms; the new tight and headline steps do not recover enough at the ad's narrowest width (394–408px). Item 19 says the step fits 'at every gated size', which is literally true (no gated size is under 1200px wide), but the regression is not in §4. It occurs in a rare window band and can be recovered from, so list it rather than block on it.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Add a §4 entry next to §4.1: 'clAInk's policy step, at 1,025 to about 1,050px wide and 620 to about 660px tall (to about 1,095 x 690 with classic scrollbars), scrolls inside the ad with Accept partly or wholly below its fold; scroll the ad or Tab to it. 2.1 showed it whole.' For a code fix instead: a sixth fit step used only on the policy step (AD_DROP gets 'brand' after 'headline', plus .claink-ad.confirming[data-fit~="brand"] .claink-ad-brand{display:none}). Injected in-page, hiding the logo row brings Accept inside the ad at 1025x640 (14px clear) and 1025x620 (1px clear) with hidden scrollbars. It is not enough with classic scrollbars, and no gated size reaches that step. Then add 1025x640 to the layout gate's dock-whole sizes. A 12px policy font would fit, but lint-css forbids anything under 13px.

verdicts.title: The release header credits Feather for 10 icons; 11 of the bundled icons are Feather-derived
verdicts.why: Line 8 of Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.1.html reads 'Lucide 1.70.0 (56 icons) ... 10 of them derived from Feather'. My script (test-results/review/layout-check/feather.mjs) lists the 56 bundled symbols and matches them against the Feather list in node_modules/lucide-static/LICENSE. By name it finds 10: arrow-right, calendar, check, compass, info, loader, lock, minus, search, x. It then compares every other bundled icon's lucide-static file with the file of every listed name, and finds exactly one more: triangle-alert. Its file is identical to alert-triangle.svg except for the class attribute, and alert-triangle is on the Feather list. The release file's i-triangle-alert symbol has those same three paths, and logLook.js uses it for risk, bad and warn log lines. So the count is 11. The count line is new in this diff (QA item 32; 2.1 credited every icon to Lucide). notices() in scripts/build.mjs matches by name only (line 133), and scripts/notices.mjs does not check the count. 'Ten' is a false statement in the shipped file's header, in QA item 32 (line 94), in QA §9 (line 477) and in CHANGELOG line 88.
verdicts.smallest_fix: In scripts/build.mjs notices(), also count a bundled icon whose lucide-static SVG, with the class attribute stripped, equals the file of a listed name (lucide-static ships the old-name files). This catches renames without an alias table. Rebuild both builds and recommit Tech_Sales_Trail_2.1.1.html: the size stays 568,319 bytes because '10' becomes '11', but the SHA-256 changes, so update it in the QA report's header table. Change 'ten' to 'eleven' in QA item 32, QA §9 and CHANGELOG.

verdicts.title: 'No hint needs a third line at any width' is false: the '+N' chip's hint takes three lines at 1025 wide, and actions §8 never points at that chip
verdicts.why: Reproduced with test-results/review/layout-check/chiphint.cjs. The state has nine chips: a competitor match (odds and a discount), a case study, conference buzz, full funnel, PIP level 2, two quad shots, a trip and rested. At 1025x768 and 1100x768 one chip shows and '+8' holds the rest. Pointing at '+8' puts 54.6px of text (three lines, starting '8 more. Discount 20% · this week · Close odds +8 pp …') in the 38.4px bar, so it runs 8.0px over the bar's top border and 8.1px over its bottom border (picture chip-nine-2.1.1-1025x768.png). It is two lines at 1180x768, 1280x720 and 1366x657. States with six or seven chips stay at two lines at 1025. 2.1 does the same thing (36px bar, 9.3px over each edge; chip-nine-2.1-1025x768.png), so the overflow is old and not a regression. What is new in this diff is the claim: QA item 12 says 'No hint needs a third line at any width of this layout', and the app.css comment says actions.cjs §8 holds that. §8 only points at the [data-act] cards, the Hail Mary, End week and the idle hint (actions.cjs lines 344–346), never at .chip.more. The claim is false for this hint. The state can be reached but needs about nine chips at once, which is very rare. CSS comments are stripped from the release file, so correcting the comment changes nothing that ships.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Change only the documents. In QA item 12 (and the app.css comment), limit the claim to the hints of the twelve actions, the Hail Mary and End week, which is what §8 measures. Add a §4 line: 'the +N chip's list of folded chips can need three lines at 1,025 to about 1,150px wide when about nine chips are in force, as in 2.1.' Adding .chip.more to §8 would make that check fail unless the code also changes.

verdicts.title: QA §4.1 understates the remaining problem: at 1025 to 1190 wide, End week hangs below the week card at every height up to about 765px, not only under 660px
verdicts.why: Reproduced with test-results/review/layout-check/grid.cjs, which measures End week's bottom against .panel.left's bottom on the 2.1.1 file. The QA's own tool state (card-fit.cjs) at 1025 and 1100px wide hangs 7.0px at 657 tall, 6.1 at 660, 7.6 at 700, 8.4 at 720, 9.5 at 746 and 0.7 at 760, and is inside from 768. midrun-seeded gives the same at 1025–1190 wide (up to 12.0px at 1190x746, 7–9.5px at 1180) and is clear from 1195. At 620px tall, End week is 32.9px past the card and 20.9px past the window for widths up to 1190, and 4px past the window at 1180–1200 depending on the state. In grid-1025x720-crop.png the card's bottom edge runs behind the Hail Mary and End week. Item 11 counts this same kind of hang (9px at 1280x720) as the 2.1 defect it fixed. §4.1 says it happens only under about 660px tall and under about 1,180px wide. §6's evidence row 'End week inside the card at every size from 1180×657 up' is also false for midrun-seeded at 1180 and 1190. The QA tool never measured 1025 or 1100 wide between 657 and 768. It is not a regression: 2.1 is worse at every one of these sizes (1025x700: 62.9px past the card and 50.9px past the window). The misstatement is new, the hang is old.
verdicts.smallest_fix: Change only the documents. Restate §4.1: 'Under about 1,200px of width (where the stat cards wrap; the exact width depends on what they say), End week and the Hail Mary hang up to about 12px through the bottom edge of the week's card at every window height up to about 765px; at 620px tall End week is also partly below the window (about 21px of its 36), still reachable by pointer and by E. 2.1 lost the button at these sizes.' In §6's evidence row, say the 1180×657-and-up result is for the card-fit tool's state.

verdicts.title: The stacked tier's caption line height (1.2) also applies to upright phones' bottom notice, which the phone tier meant to keep as it was
verdicts.why: Reproduced with test-results/review/layout-check/caption.cjs on touch contexts, raising lines with TST_AUDIO.say. At 390x844 and 360x640 the bottom notice's computed line height is 18.2px in 2.1 and 15.6px in 2.1.1. Two-line notices (whale, meetings, freeze) shrink from 54.4px to 51.2px. On the intended targets, an upright tablet (768x1024) and a sideways phone (844x390), the caption is in the top bar as item 17 says. Cause: the stacked tier's .pa-cap{white-space:normal;line-height:1.2} (app.css:235) also matches phones. The phone tier (app.css:280–281) resets display, overflow and line-clamp but not line-height. So this is an unintended, unlisted change to how every phone caption looks. Nothing is cut, and the peek's 60px offset still clears a two-line notice, so it is cosmetic and a player would not see anything broken. The reviewer's second option (scoping the rule to .topbar .pa-cap) would not work: the phone's notice is a fixed-position child of .topbar (measured: closest('.topbar') is true at 390x844).
verdicts.smallest_fix: Add line-height:1.4 to the phone tier's .pa-cap rule (app.css:280). Injected in-page (caption-fix.cjs), it restores 18.2px line height and 54.4px notices at 390x844 and 360x640, and leaves the tablet and sideways-phone top bar at 15.6px. Include it in the rebuild that the Feather count needs anyway; otherwise list it in §4.
